significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) ordering and intervention interaction: for matched initial misalignment and repair budget, subliminally installed misalignment declines more slowly under content-based re-alignment, while "directly ablating the shared toxic-persona direction removes both channels comparably"; the proposed early-layer coupling would additionally predict repair resistance. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining expected repair-dose curves and distinguishing content-access resistance from intrinsically harder-to-remove or off-direction misalignment; Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning work makes persistence of covertly transmitted traits a concrete issue, although I could not independently verify the recent arXiv:2605.12798 record as of 2026-08-27. True and false are distinguishable, and a null would rule against channel-specific resistance within the stated repair methods and model scope, though it would not establish universal removability. After substituting the claim with the generic topic "extend subliminal learning," I would not retain this score: the matched-channel decay ordering plus equal-ablation/content-repair dissociation is substantially more constraining than the obvious first hypothesis that subliminal traits persist or can be removed.

reach.justification: The principal handles are the "budget to reach M <= 5 pp," the proposed relation that "early-layer concentration predicts resistance out-of-sample," and "DIRECT toxic-persona-direction ablation" as an intervention when ordinary content repair leaves a residual. Early-layer concentration is potentially ex ante because it can forecast the required repair budget before remediation is attempted, while residual harmful rate is post hoc and direct ablation is a remedial rather than predictive handle. If the predictive coupling is verified, re-extraction on another model should recover an expected concentration-resistance relation rather than merely a new direction to inspect, but the broader ablation finding still requires model-specific direction extraction and the hypothesis does not clearly assert architecture-wide invariance. Downstream users plausibly include "model-distillation vendors, enterprise fine-tuning teams, and evaluation/auditing groups" that could choose stronger repair, ablation, or quarantine; the topic-substitution check lowers none of this credit because generic subliminal learning alone supplies neither an advance warning metric nor a channel-specific remediation rule.
